result.topic_en: Euler tabulates the system of equations for the order m+n=15, with coefficients written as sums of binomial numbers so that they follow a common law. He then proposes to remove the doubts of the induction by using odd instead of even powers of p.

items.quote: Atque nunc lex progressionis non nimis est complexa, eamque facile ad altiores ordines accommodare licet.
items.english: And now the law of the progression is not too complicated, and it can easily be adapted to higher orders.

items.quote: Cum autem haec lex, quatenus inductioni innititur, minus certa videri posset, omnia plane dubia tollentur, si loco potestatum parium ipsius $p$ impares introducantur.
items.english: But since this law, insofar as it rests on induction, might seem less certain, all doubts will be completely removed if odd powers of p are introduced in place of the even ones.
